p01.why: The block declares value as a variable and then as a function, two different entities with one name in one block.

p02.why: x = 2 assigns the outer x before the inner x is declared, the innermost block sees inner x = 3 so y = 30 and its own x = 31, and the outer x stays 2.

p03.why: Null statements, a for loop with a null body, and an empty block are all valid statements.

p04.why: Empty and nested blocks and null statements are valid, and the two increments run in order, so n is 2.

p05.why: Both expression statements evaluate tick() and discard the value; the unused value can only draw a warning, and no -Werror is given.

p06.why: x is declared twice in one block as two different variables.

p07.why: The variable Point hides the class, struct Point still names the class, and 3 + 4 is 7.

p08.why: x is declared twice in one block.

p09.why: inner is visible only to the end of its nested block, so return inner names nothing.

p10.why: Maker(x) looks like a declaration, but -> cannot continue one, so the statement is an expression that sets global.v to 5.

p11.why: The cast to void silences the unused-value warning, so -Werror has nothing to turn into an error.

p12.why: Repeated function declarations, repeated extern declarations of one variable, and repeated typedefs of one type are all allowed in a block.

p13.why: A label can come before a declaration, and the goto lands before the declaration, so x is initialized to 4 and n becomes 4.

p14.why: Statements, including the one in the nested block, run in written order.

p15.why: Declarations run their initializers when reached, so mark is called with 1, 2, 3, 4 in order.

p16.why: After int Point the name Point alone means the variable, so Point p{4} cannot name the class.

p17.why: Naming the volatile flag reads it, which is valid; flag is 1, so main returns 0.

p18.why: int(x); is a declaration of a new inner x, so x = 5 changes the inner x and the outer x stays 1.

p19.why: The two typedefs give Count two different types in one block.

p20.why: The inner x hides the outer x only inside the nested block.

p21.why: Each of the four statements can be read as a declaration with parentheses around the declarator, so they declare b, c, p, and d with the expected values.

p22.why: A case label as the last item of a switch body is valid; Clang and EDG accept it and GCC rejects it (Q-0096).

p23.why: A plain label can be the last item of a block; the Evidence names only case and default labels as the GCC disagreement.

p25.why: a + 1 has no effect and its value is unused, so Clang and GCC warn under -Wunused-value and -Werror makes the warning an error.

p26.why: A default label as the last item of a switch body is valid; Clang and EDG accept it and GCC rejects it (Q-0096).
